    Estimate whole-frame MSSR resources

    Source: R/resources.R
    mssr_estimate_resources.Rd

    Reports a conservative allocation model before allocating an output frame. The estimate includes a 128 MiB runtime allowance, 24 double buffers per output pixel, six per input pixel, and reflected-index and offset storage. It was calibrated on the peak resident memory of fresh R processes on one Linux machine over a workload ladder of 65,536 to 16,777,216 output pixels (amplification 1 to 4, orders 0 to 3, mesh and intensity weighting on and off, disk and square kernels), where it exceeded every measured peak by 30 to 220 percent; the margin is smallest for order 3 with mesh and weighting, and garbage-collection timing changes peaks from run to run. It is a planning guard, not a hard process-memory limit: other platforms, loaded packages, retained objects, garbage collection and the allocator can change peak RSS, and estimates outside that ladder are extrapolations.

    Usage

    mssr_estimate_resources(
  input_dim,
  fwhm,
  amp = 1L,
  kernel = c("disk", "square"),
  rounding = c("half_even", "half_up"),
  max_output_pixels = 5e+07,
  frames = NULL,
  statistic = NULL
)

    Arguments

    input_dim

    Two positive whole numbers: input rows and columns.

    fwhm, amp, kernel, rounding, max_output_pixels

    As in mssr().

    frames, statistic

    Optional: the number of frames and the statistic of a temporal call (see mssr_temporal()). Give both or neither.

    Value

    A list with input/output dimensions, pixels, offsets, estimated work, estimated peak bytes, model ID, and limitations; with frames and statistic, also the temporal estimates described above.

    Details

    With frames and statistic, the list also estimates a call of mssr_temporal() (model temporal_buffers_v3): stack_bytes for the stored per-frame maps, stored_peak_bytes and recompute_peak_bytes for its two computation paths (the single-frame peak plus the output-sized buffers each path holds, the raw temporal mean and one raw frame), and the total neighborhood work of each path. The stored path counts the maps twice (a 100 percent margin): R lets garbage accumulate in proportion to the live heap before it collects, and on long stored stacks the measured peak came close to twice the bare map size. The input array is read frame by frame and not copied, so it is not counted. The per-frame limits of mssr() apply to every frame.

    Examples

    mssr_estimate_resources(c(128, 192), fwhm = 3, amp = 2)
#> $input_dim
#> [1] 128 192
#> 
#> $output_dim
#> [1] 256 384
#> 
#> $output_pixels
#> [1] 98304
#> 
#> $half_size
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $n_offsets
#> [1] 28
#> 
#> $estimated_work
#> [1] 2752512
#> 
#> $estimated_peak_bytes
#> [1] 154291456
#> 
#> $model
#> [1] "whole_frame_buffers_v2"
#> 
#> $hard_limit
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $limitation
#> [1] "Allocation estimate; retained objects and runtime can increase process RSS."
#> 
mssr_estimate_resources(c(128, 192), fwhm = 3, amp = 2, frames = 100, statistic = "var")
